subject: Pre-cutover BGP/MTU/sidecar readiness & traffic-shift plan
messages:
From: Lauren Greer <lgreer@acme-infra.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: ACME Network Ops <netops@acme-infra.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pre-cutover checklist: BGP path confirmation, MTU validation and sidecar behavior

Team —

Thanks for the sync this morning. Per our prep call, attaching the BGP trace from the spine->edge session, and the preliminary MTU test results from the staging rack. High-level items we observed: 

- BGP: primary path is stable, but we see intermittent AS-PATH prepend from peer-2 around 08:25PT (attached acme-bgp-trace-20261130.txt).
- MTU: jumbo frames (9000) pass within the data center fabric, but there is a consistent 1462 MTU observed across the transit VPN egress (see mtu-validation-summary-20261130.pdf).
- Sidecars: our initial ISTIO-injection smoke showed proxy-initialization taking 1.2s on average for the 4-node canary. We captured logs in the sidecar-injection-checklist.md.

Two asks before we move to traffic shift: 
1) Redwood: confirm that your deployment will honor a 1462 path MTU without fragmentation — specifically the native gRPC keepalive + payloads we use for K/V warmups.
2) Ops: can Redwood provide a short runbook snippet for emergency rollback if sidecar mis-injection causes 5xx spikes? Prefer a single-step hit to detach the sidecar or fallback to host networking.

We propose a 10% traffic shift at 18:00PT with a 30-minute watch window if both checks pass. Please reply with confirmations and any additional evidence you need.

—Lauren
Lauren Greer
Senior Infrastructure Manager, ACME Infrastructure
Attachments: acme-bgp-trace-20261130.txt (text), mtu-validation-summary-20261130.pdf (pdf), sidecar-injection-checklist.md (text)
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Lauren Greer <lgreer@acme-infra.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pre-cutover checklist: BGP path confirmation, MTU validation and sidecar behavior

Lauren —

Thanks for the artifacts, very helpful. Short answers up front: 

1) MTU handling: Redwood runtime will respect a 1462 effective path MTU. We will set TCP MSS clamp to 1442 on the egress host interfaces for the cutover window, and we have validated reassembly behavior in our staging harness. Evidence: attached runbook-cutover-appendix-A.txt contains the exact iptables/MSS commands we will run.

2) Sidecar rollback: we have a 2-step emergency rollback for sidecar regressions: 
   - Step A: toggle redwood-runtime flag to disable automatic sidecar injection for the affected namespace (single CLI call, < 10s).
   - Step B: if errors persist, an automated job will cordon the canary podset and restart pods with host network config (takes ~60–120s).

Action items I assigned in-line: 
- laura_bennett: please validate that the MSS-clamp change does not conflict with ACME transit ACLs.
- marcus_lin: run a controlled 150MB payload test over the transit path at 14:00PT and post results to the Drive folder.
- rishi_malhotra: prepare a short prom alert rule for sidecar-init latency > 2s during the watch window.

If all green, we are comfortable with the 10% traffic bump at 18:00PT; we will hold full-shift until 2h stable.

Hannah Schmitt
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
Attachments: runbook-cutover-appendix-A.txt (text)
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Lauren Greer <lgreer@acme-infra.com>, ACME Network Ops <netops@acme-infra.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pre-cutover checklist: BGP path confirmation, MTU validation and sidecar behavior

Quick update from the payload test (14:00PT): 

- 150MB end-to-end transfer completed with TCP segmentation adjusted; no packet loss observed at the application layer. Wire capture shows fragmentation at 1462 and proper reassembly at the destination. Attached short log/snippet to Drive.
- I validated MSS clamp on a test host; command we used: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1442`. No adverse flags from transit.
- Sidecar latency: saw 1.4s cold start for the injected proxy on node-3 (extra 0.2s vs earlier). Rishi — can you add a temporary alert for sidecar-init > 1.8s instead of 2s so we get earlier warning?

Recommendation: proceed with 10% shift at 18:00PT, enact MSS clamp at 17:45PT, and have the sidecar-disable CLI ready (one-liner included in runbook appendix). I will be on the bridge from 17:30PT.

Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Greer <lgreer@acme-infra.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: ACME Network Ops <netops@acme-infra.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pre-cutover checklist: BGP path confirmation, MTU validation and sidecar behavior

Thanks, all — that aligns with our ops expectations. 

Confirming: ACME will accept the 10% traffic shift at 18:00PT with the MSS clamp and rollback plan in place. Our NetOps team will monitor BGP AS-PATH anomalies and hold a separate ticket for the prepend behavior; they will not block the shift unless a hard route flap occurs. 

I'll sign the cutover acknowledgement and place the DocuSign link in the Drive folder. See you on the bridge at 17:30PT.

—Lauren
